result.title: Bridging CLIP with DINO: Cross-Modal Information Maximization for Online Test-Time Adaptation
result.summary: Vision-language models such as CLIP enable zero-shot classification from arbitrary class names, but under test-time corruptions, their visual encoder projects distorted features onto incorrect textual anchors with high confidence: a phenomenon we term modality bias. Standard entropy minimization reinforces these overconfident errors, which creates a confirmation-bias loop and collapses the predicted label distribution. We propose an online test-time adaptation (TTA) method that breaks this loop at three levels. At the representation level, a frozen self-supervised backbone (e.g., DINO v2) is combined with CLIP through a cross-covariance logit ensemble. CLIP text prototypes are projected into the feature space of this text-free backbone, so the self-supervised branch classifies native image features and is less affected by the text bias of CLIP. At the optimization level, a gated test-time information-maximization objective pairs per-sample sharpening with batch-level diversity, while an adaptive gate excludes unreliable samples from the gradient. At the prediction level, an online logit adjustment corrects the residual class-distribution skew. CDIM outperforms the compared CLIP-based online TTA baselines on ImageNet-C, CIFAR10-C, and CIFAR100-C, and remains competitive in continual and mixed-domain TTA. Extensive analyses and ablation studies verify the contribution of each of its components. Our code is available at https://github.com/B1ueC1oud/CDIM

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 CLIP 在测试时损坏下出现的「模态偏置」现象（视觉特征被高置信投影到错误文本锚点），提出在线 TTA 方法 CDIM：融合冻结自监督 DINOv2 分支与跨协方差 logit 集成，并配合门控信息最大化目标与在线 logit 调整。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「文本偏置导致预测分布坍缩」诊断与用无文本自监督分支绕过语言先验的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据是否真正参与、以及不可靠样本的门控监督提供线索，可供核查。
